newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon interest rates to fall slightly-c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon interest rates to fall slightly-c.bank.

text.p: Lebanese interest rates are currently at an acceptable level but will fall slightly in the next few months, Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh said on Wednesday.

"The current interest rates characterised by stability at the February 1997 level are acceptable rates and they are expected to fall within narrow margins in the coming months," Salameh said in an address to Arab bankers and financiers.
Rates on government treasury bills dropped sharply for several months until February. Since then shorter-term rates have inched down while longer-term rates have remained steady.
Yields currently range from 13.66 percent for three-month bills to 16.08 for two-year paper.
The reductions are seen as an attempt by the government to reduce its massive debt servicing costs and stimulate the economy.
The Lebanese Banks Association has also slashed interest rates recently on bank loans in line with government rates.
